answer: Each identity claims one meadow plot, locks a 70-credit bond, and files a bridge tally: a turnstile counts animals crossing the bridge, and kernel feed is issued per crossing, 12 kernel units. An auditor recomputes feed from bridge tally and stock depletion; a shortfall, reused tally, or second plot under one key burns the bond. First plot costs 31, the kth 31+6(k-1), the 1000th 6025, so 1000 fakes pay 3,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-herd ring fails: rented animals carry the lender key, so counts do not match the meadow. An honest keeper pays 31 once and keeps the bond after audit.
